summary: Upgraded the ClientApp from Angular 10.2 to Angular 11.2 with `ng update @angular/core@11 @angular/cli@11`, which ran all of Angular's v11 migrations (waitForAsync rename in the specs, explicit `relativeLinkResolution: 'legacy'` on RouterModule.forRoot, removal of the dropped `extractCss` builder option) and moved the karma/jasmine tooling to their v11 baselines. NgRx was bumped 10.1 -> 11.1 because NgRx 10 peers only with Angular 10. `npm install` and `npm run build` pass; `npm test` still fails for the same pre-existing angular.json misconfiguration it failed with at baseline.
changes: Ran `ng update @angular/core@11 @angular/cli@11 --allow-dirty --force`; all v11 migrations ran (AbstractControl.parent non-null, ViewEncapsulation.Native, NavigationExtras omissions/preserveQueryParams, RouterModule initialNavigation, relativeLinkResolution, async -> waitForAsync, canActivate+redirectTo).
angular.json: the v11 migration removed the now-invalid `extractCss` option from both the base build options and the `production` configuration (CSS extraction is unconditional in v11).
src/app/app.module.ts: `RouterModule.forRoot(...)` now passes `{ relativeLinkResolution: 'legacy' }` explicitly, pinning the pre-v11 behaviour so routing is unchanged.
The three component specs (add-employee, counter, fetch-employee) now import and use `waitForAsync` instead of the deprecated `async` testing helper.
Ran `ng update @ngrx/store@11`, moving all five @ngrx packages from 10.1.2 to 11.1.1 (NgRx 10 peer-restricts @angular/core to ^10.0.0); no NgRx source migrations were needed.
TypeScript stays at 4.0.8, which Angular 11 supports; no TS bump was required this hop.
package-lock.json regenerated through npm; verified with a clean `rm -rf node_modules && npm install` (exit 0) followed by a passing `npm run build` (exit 0).
manual_followups: `npm test` fails at baseline and still fails with the identical cause: the karma target in angular.json lists `"styles": ["styles.css"]` instead of `"src/styles.css"`, so the builder cannot resolve the entry (ENOENT on ClientApp/styles.css). Pre-existing, not a regression; worth fixing so the suite can actually run.

@nguniversal/module-map-ngfactory-loader is still pinned at 7.1.0 and warns about incompatible @angular/{common,core,platform-server} peers. With Ivy the ModuleMapLoaderModule is obsolete; src/app/app.server.module.ts should drop it and the package should be removed. This will become a hard blocker at the hop that needs a real @nguniversal bump.
The build still emits `src/main.ts depends on '@angular/platform-server'. CommonJS or AMD dependencies can cause optimization bailouts.` Harmless; silenceable via `allowedCommonJsDependencies`.

node-sass 4.11 (an optionalDependency) still fails to compile on this Node 12 / Python 3 image and is skipped. Nothing in the build uses Sass, so it blocks nothing, but it should be removed or replaced with `sass`.
`ng update` had to be run with NG_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 from a CLI 11 install in /tmp: without it the local CLI fetches the latest stable CLI, which refuses to run on Node 12.
`ng update` relaxed codelyzer from ^6.0.2 to ^6.0.0; the lockfile still resolves 6.0.2, so this is cosmetic. codelyzer/tslint are deprecated and should be replaced with ESLint in a later hop.
